logic_node.action: Administer continuous IV inotropic support as bridge therapy
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with advanced (stage D) HF refractory to GDMT and device therapy who are eligible for and awaiting MCS or cardiac transplantation, continuous intravenous inotropic support is reasonable as bridge therapy.

source_text: In patients with advanced (stage D) HF refractory to GDMT and device therapy who are eligible for and awaiting MCS or cardiac transplantation, continuous intravenous inotropic support is reasonable as 'bridge therapy.'

logic_node.action: Consider continuous IV inotropic support as palliative therapy
logic_node.action_detail: In select patients with stage D HF, despite optimal GDMT and device therapy who are ineligible for either MCS or cardiac transplantation, continuous intravenous inotropic support may be considered as palliative therapy for symptom control and improvement in functional status.

source_text: In select patients with stage D HF, despite optimal GDMT and device therapy who are ineligible for either MCS or cardiac transplantation, continuous intravenous inotropic support may be considered as palliative therapy for symptom control.

logic_node.action: Avoid long-term continuous or intermittent IV inotropes
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HF, long-term use of either continuous or intermittent intravenous inotropic agents, for reasons other than palliative care or as a bridge to advanced therapies, is potentially harmful.

source_text: In patients with HF, long-term use of either continuous or intermittent intravenous inotropic agents, for reasons other than palliative care or as a bridge to advanced therapies, is potentially harmful.

logic_node.action: Administer dopamine at inotropic dose range
logic_node.action_detail: Dopamine: no bolus, infusion 5-10 mcg/kg/min for inotropic effect (increases CO and HR, neutral SVR/PVR); at 10-15 mcg/kg/min adds vasopressor effect (increases SVR). Half-life 2-20 min, metabolized renally/hepatically/plasma. Adverse effects: tachyarrhythmias, headache, nausea, tissue necrosis. Caution with MAO inhibitors.

source_text: Dopamine: NA bolus, infusion 5-10 mcg/kg/min, t1/2 2-20 min, increases CO and HR, neutral SVR/PVR. At 10-15 mcg/kg/min increases SVR. Adverse: T, HA, N, tissue necrosis. Caution: MAO-I.

logic_node.action: Administer dobutamine infusion
logic_node.action_detail: Dobutamine: no bolus, infusion 2.5-20 mcg/kg/min. Half-life 2-3 min, hepatic metabolism. Increases CO and HR, neutral SVR/PVR. Adverse effects: BP changes, headache, tachyarrhythmias, nausea, fever, hypersensitivity. Caution with MAO inhibitors. Contraindicated in sulfite allergy.

source_text: Dobutamine: NA bolus, infusion 2.5-20 mcg/kg/min, t1/2 2-3 min hepatic. Increases CO, HR. Neutral SVR, PVR. Adverse: BP changes, HA, T, N, F, hypersensitivity. Caution: MAO-I; CI: sulfite allergy.

logic_node.action: Administer milrinone infusion
logic_node.action_detail: Milrinone (PDE3 inhibitor): bolus not recommended, infusion 0.125-0.75 mcg/kg/min. Half-life 2.5 hours, hepatic metabolism. Increases CO and HR, decreases SVR and PVR. Adverse effects: tachyarrhythmias, hypotension. Accumulates in renal failure; monitor kidney function and LFTs.

source_text: Milrinone: NR bolus, infusion 0.125-0.75 mcg/kg/min, t1/2 2.5h hepatic. Increases CO, HR. Decreases SVR, PVR. Adverse: T, decreased BP. Accumulation in renal failure; monitor kidney function and LFTs.

logic_node.action: Administer epinephrine infusion
logic_node.action_detail: Epinephrine: bolus not recommended. Low-dose infusion 5-15 mcg/min increases CO and HR with variable SVR effect. High-dose 15-20 mcg/min produces marked increases in HR and SVR. Half-life 2-3 min. Adverse effects: headache, tachyarrhythmias. Caution with MAO inhibitors.

source_text: Epinephrine: NR bolus, 5-15 mcg/min increases CO/HR, variable SVR. 15-20 mcg/min markedly increases HR and SVR. t1/2 2-3 min. Adverse: HA, T. Caution: MAO-I.

logic_node.action: Administer norepinephrine infusion
logic_node.action_detail: Norepinephrine: bolus not recommended, infusion 0.5-30 mcg/min. Half-life 2.5 min. Neutral effect on CO, increases HR and markedly increases SVR, neutral PVR. Adverse effects: decreased HR (reflex), tissue necrosis. Caution with MAO inhibitors.

source_text: Norepinephrine: NR bolus, infusion 0.5-30 mcg/min, t1/2 2.5 min. Neutral CO, increases HR, markedly increases SVR. Adverse: decreased HR, tissue necrosis. Caution: MAO-I.

logic_node.action: Use lower inotrope doses and reassess ongoing need
logic_node.action_detail: To minimize adverse effects, lower doses of parenteral inotropic drugs are preferred. Tachyphylaxis should be acknowledged and agent may need to be changed during longer support. The ongoing need for inotropic support and possibility of discontinuation should be regularly assessed.

source_text: To minimize adverse effects, lower doses of parenteral inotropic drugs are preferred...the ongoing need for inotropic support and the possibility of discontinuation should be regularly assessed.

logic_node.action: Monitor kidney function and LFTs during milrinone infusion
logic_node.action_detail: Milrinone accumulates in the setting of renal failure. Monitor kidney function and liver function tests during milrinone infusion. Consider dose adjustment or alternative agent in patients with renal impairment.

source_text: Accumulation may occur in setting of renal failure; monitor kidney function and LFTs.

logic_node.action: Implant durable LVAD
logic_node.action_detail: In select patients with advanced HFrEF with NYHA class IV symptoms who are deemed dependent on continuous intravenous inotropes or temporary MCS, durable LVAD implantation is effective to improve functional status, QOL, and survival. Two-year survival >80% with newer generation LVADs.

source_text: In select patients with advanced HFrEF with NYHA class IV symptoms who are deemed dependent on continuous intravenous inotropes or temporary MCS, durable LVAD implantation is effective to improve functional status, QOL, and survival.

logic_node.action: Consider durable MCS despite GDMT
logic_node.action_detail: In select patients with advanced HFrEF who have NYHA class IV symptoms despite GDMT, durable MCS can be beneficial to improve symptoms, improve functional class, and reduce mortality. Destination therapy MCS provides considerable survival advantage plus improvement in functional status and health-related QOL.

source_text: In select patients with advanced HFrEF who have NYHA class IV symptoms despite GDMT, durable MCS can be beneficial to improve symptoms, improve functional class, and reduce mortality.

logic_node.action: Consider temporary MCS as bridge to recovery or decision
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with advanced HFrEF and hemodynamic compromise and shock, temporary MCS, including percutaneous and extracorporeal ventricular assist devices, are reasonable as a bridge to recovery or bridge to decision.

source_text: In patients with advanced HFrEF and hemodynamic compromise and shock, temporary MCS, including percutaneous and extracorporeal ventricular assist devices, are reasonable as a 'bridge to recovery' or 'bridge to decision.'

logic_node.action: Identify indications for durable MCS
logic_node.action_detail: Indications for durable MCS (combination required): frequent hospitalizations for HF, NYHA class IIIb-IV despite maximal therapy, intolerance of neurohormonal antagonists, increasing diuretic requirement, symptomatic despite CRT, inotrope dependence, low peak VO2 (<14-16 mL/kg/min), end-organ dysfunction attributable to low cardiac output.

source_text: Indications: frequent HF hospitalizations, NYHA IIIb-IV despite maximal therapy, intolerance of neurohormonal antagonists, increasing diuretic requirement, symptomatic despite CRT, inotrope dependence, low peak VO2 (<14-16).

logic_node.action: Identify absolute contraindications to durable MCS
logic_node.action_detail: Absolute contraindications to durable MCS: irreversible hepatic disease, irreversible renal disease, irreversible neurological disease, medical nonadherence, severe psychosocial limitations.

source_text: Absolute contraindications: irreversible hepatic disease, irreversible renal disease, irreversible neurological disease, medical nonadherence, severe psychosocial limitations.

logic_node.action: Identify relative contraindication: age >80 for destination therapy MCS
logic_node.action_detail: Relative contraindications to durable MCS include: age >80 years for destination therapy, obesity or malnutrition, musculoskeletal disease impairing rehabilitation, active systemic infection or prolonged intubation, untreated malignancy, severe PVD, active substance abuse, impaired cognitive function, unmanaged psychiatric disorder, lack of social support.

source_text: Relative contraindications: age >80y for destination therapy, obesity or malnutrition, musculoskeletal disease, active infection, untreated malignancy, severe PVD, active substance abuse, impaired cognition, unmanaged psychiatric disorder, lack of social support.

logic_node.action: Continue and uptitrate GDMT after durable MCS implantation
logic_node.action_detail: Continuing and uptitrating guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) in patients with durable MCS is recommended. GDMT optimization should continue after LVAD implantation.

source_text: Continuing and uptitrating GDMT in patients with durable MCS is recommended.

logic_node.action: Acknowledge excess morbidity with MCS if unable to tolerate anticoagulation
logic_node.action_detail: In patients who are unable to tolerate anticoagulation after repeated challenges, implantation of a durable MCS is associated with excess morbidity. Pump thrombosis, hemolysis, and ischemic neurologic events have been linked to subtherapeutic INR.

source_text: In patients who are unable to tolerate anticoagulation after repeated challenges, implantation of a durable MCS is associated with excess morbidity; pump thrombosis, hemolysis, and ischemic neurologic events linked to subtherapeutic INR.

logic_node.action: Refer for cardiac transplantation
logic_node.action_detail: For selected patients with advanced HF despite GDMT, cardiac transplantation is indicated to improve survival and QOL. Median survival of adult transplant recipients is now >12 years; 1, 3, and 5-year survival is 90.3%, 84.7%, and 79.6% respectively.

source_text: For selected patients with advanced HF despite GDMT, cardiac transplantation is indicated to improve survival and QOL. Median survival now >12 years.

logic_node.action: Use IV inotropic support to maintain systemic perfusion
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with cardiogenic shock, intravenous inotropic support should be used to maintain systemic perfusion and preserve end-organ performance. No robust evidence for superiority of one inotrope over another. Agent choice guided by blood pressure, concurrent arrhythmias, and drug availability.

source_text: In patients with cardiogenic shock, intravenous inotropic support should be used to maintain systemic perfusion and preserve end-organ performance. There is a lack of robust evidence to suggest the clear benefit of one inotropic agent over another.

logic_node.action: Consider temporary MCS when pharmacologic support insufficient
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with cardiogenic shock, temporary MCS is reasonable when end-organ function cannot be maintained by pharmacologic means to support cardiac function.

source_text: In patients with cardiogenic shock, temporary MCS is reasonable when end-organ function cannot be maintained by pharmacologic means to support cardiac function.

logic_node.action: Manage with multidisciplinary shock team
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with cardiogenic shock, management by a multidisciplinary team experienced in shock is reasonable. Shock team use was associated with improved 30-day all-cause mortality (HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.41-0.93) and reduced in-hospital mortality (61.0% vs 47.9%).

source_text: In patients with cardiogenic shock, management by a multidisciplinary team experienced in shock is reasonable. Shock team use associated with improved 30-day mortality (HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.41-0.93).

logic_node.action: Consider PA catheterization for hemodynamic assessment
logic_node.action_detail: In patients presenting with cardiogenic shock, placement of a PA catheter may be considered to define hemodynamic subsets and guide management strategies. PA catheterization is particularly useful when there is diagnostic uncertainty about cause of hypotension or end-organ dysfunction, or when patient is not responding to initial shock measures.

source_text: In patients presenting with cardiogenic shock, placement of a PA line may be considered to define hemodynamic subsets and appropriate management strategies. PA catheterization may also be useful when there is diagnostic uncertainty.

logic_node.action: Consider early transfer to MCS-capable center
logic_node.action_detail: For patients who are not rapidly responding to initial shock measures, triage to centers that can provide temporary MCS may be considered to optimize management. Transfer should be considered early when trajectory shows worsening end-organ malperfusion.

source_text: For patients who are not rapidly responding to initial shock measures, triage to centers that can provide temporary MCS may be considered to optimize management.

logic_node.action: Apply cardiogenic shock diagnostic criteria
logic_node.action_detail: Cardiogenic shock diagnosis requires: SBP <90 mmHg for >30 min (or MAP <60 mmHg, or vasopressor requirement to maintain SBP >=90 or MAP >=60) PLUS hypoperfusion (decreased mentation, cold extremities/livedo, urine output <30 mL/h, or lactate >2 mmol/L) PLUS cardiac index <2.0 L/min/m2.

source_text: Shock requires SBP <90 mmHg for >30 min, or MAP <60 for >30 min, or vasopressor use AND hypoperfusion (decreased mentation, cold extremities, UO <30 mL/h, lactate >2 mmol/L) AND cardiac index <2.0 L/min/m2.

logic_node.action: Apply shock hemodynamic criteria
logic_node.action_detail: Hemodynamic criteria for cardiogenic shock: SBP <90 mmHg or MAP <60 mmHg, cardiac index <2.2 L/min/m2, pulmonary capillary wedge pressure >15 mmHg. Additional considerations: cardiac power output <0.6W, shock index (HR/SBP) >1.0, RV shock markers including PAP pulsatility index and CVP >15 mmHg.

source_text: Hemodynamic criteria: SBP <90 or MAP <60, CI <2.2, PCWP >15 mmHg. Additional: CPO <0.6W, shock index >1.0, RV shock: PAPi, CVP >15 mmHg, CVP-PCW >0.6.

logic_node.action: Classify cardiogenic shock by SCAI stages
logic_node.action_detail: SCAI cardiogenic shock staging: Stage A (at risk): normotensive, normal perfusion, normal labs. Stage B (beginning/pre-shock): hypotension, preserved perfusion, SBP <90 or MAP <60. Stage C (classic): hypotension + hypoperfusion, impaired renal function, increased lactate, CI <=2.2, PCWP >15, CPO <0.6W. Stage D (deteriorating): worsening of stage C with escalating pressors/MCS. Stage E (extremis): refractory shock, cardiac arrest.

source_text: SCAI stages: A=at risk, B=beginning shock (SBP<90, MAP<60, CI>=2.2), C=classic (hypoperfusion, CI<=2.2, PCWP>15, CPO<0.6W), D=deteriorating (escalating pressors/MCS), E=extremis (cardiac arrest).

logic_node.action: Use caution combining inotropes with MAO inhibitors
logic_node.action_detail: Caution is required when using dopamine, dobutamine, epinephrine, or norepinephrine in patients taking monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAO-I). MAO inhibitors can potentiate the effects of catecholamines and adrenergic agonists.

source_text: Dopamine, Dobutamine, Epinephrine, Norepinephrine: Caution with MAO-I.

logic_node.action: Avoid dobutamine in sulfite allergy
logic_node.action_detail: Dobutamine is contraindicated in patients with sulfite allergy.

source_text: Dobutamine: CI: sulfite allergy.

logic_node.action: Counsel on arrhythmia and infection risks with palliative inotropes
logic_node.action_detail: The use of inotropes for palliation carries risks for arrhythmias and catheter-related infections. The presence of an ICD decreases mortality associated with arrhythmias. This risk should be shared with patients, especially if planned inotrope use in a patient without an ICD or in whom the preference is to deactivate the ICD for palliative purposes.

source_text: Use of inotropes for palliation carries risks for arrhythmias and catheter-related infections. Presence of an ICD decreases mortality associated with arrhythmias. Risk should be shared with patients.

logic_node.action: Use MCS to reverse transplant-ineligibility conditions
logic_node.action_detail: For patients initially considered transplant-ineligible because of pulmonary hypertension, obesity, overall frailty, or other reasons, MCS can provide time to reverse or modify these conditions and allow subsequent transplant eligibility.

source_text: For patients initially considered transplant-ineligible because of pulmonary hypertension, obesity, overall frailty, or other reasons, MCS can provide time to reverse or modify these conditions.
